manifest.approach: Matching decompilation with GCC 2.95.2 (USA) and GCC 2.8.1 (Japan, Europe), splat and maspsx, byte-identical for all three releases from one source tree
manifest.notes: Every game function is C in all three releases, the executable and the overlays: 1,370 functions in the USA one, 1,191 in the Japanese one and 1,598 in the European one. The game's data is C too, and each release rebuilds byte for byte, checked against the SHA-1 of every original binary. The PsyQ libraries are Sony's code, not the game's, and are left out of the progress. Readability work continues: names, comments and cleaner C. 7 functions still match through a fake match, each marked in the source and listed in TODO.md.

The CPU rasteriser samples the same decoded texture and paints the same pixel, so the two back ends disagree about one combiner, not about the data. manifest.approach: Matching decompilation with GCC 2.8.1, splat and maspsx, byte-identical main executable and 7 stage overlays
manifest.notes: All 1,088 game functions are matched C: the main executable SLUS_011.93 and the 7 stage overlays (STAG0000 to STAG4000.PRO) rebuild byte for byte, checked against the SHA-1 of each retail file. Functions, globals and struct fields are named where the code proves them, and doc/STATE_MAP.md maps every global. The build is shiftable, so the C can be changed and relinked. The PsyQ libraries are Sony's code, not the game's, and stay as split asm outside the progress.

manifest.approach: Static recompilation of the main executable with PS2Recomp, plus a native layer that draws with the PC GPU and handles sound, FMVs and input instead of emulating the VU1, GS and IOP. A readable C++ de
manifest.notes: The recompiled C++ is game code and is generated locally from your own disc, so it is not in the repo. Playable on Windows (releases ship with a mod kit), with a Linux x86-64 port in the tree. Mods (PNG textures, skins, custom monsters, custom stages) go in the mods folder, and there is a level editor. Decomp functions are byte-matched where cheap, the rest are kept as functionally equivalent C++ and marked NON_MATCHING. SDK and PS2 hardware code is skipped, since the port replaces it.
